Check one spec item against the schema

Source: R/schema.R
tfl_schema_check.Rd

One item of a spec's content: (tfl_item()): its function is one the schema or its package knows; each argument is the function's (its formals, or the grammar of its ...); each value has the argument's type. What the reader of a spec file calls on every item, and what the AI review reports.

Usage

tfl_schema_check(item)

Arguments

item

A tfl_item() (or a list with fn and args).

Value

The problems: a data frame (fn, arg, level – "error" or "warning" – and message), no rows when the item is fine.

Details

An argument the function does not have is a warning, not an error: the last word is the installed package's formals when the code runs (a newer package may have it). An argument the schema marks renamed_to says what it is now and since which version, in the words the GUI's suggestion and the AI review also use.

See also

tfl_schema()

Examples

tfl_schema_check(tfl_item("plan_sort", list(keys = c("-n", "SOC"))))
#> [1] fn      arg     level   message
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
tfl_schema_check(tfl_item("plan_sort", list(keys = c("-n"), sort = 1)))
#>          fn  arg   level
#> 1 plan_sort sort warning
#>                                                       message
#> 1 plan_sort has no argument `sort` (it has: stat, keep, keys)
